answer: Randomness-gated admission caps. Each epoch, agents submit identity claims hashed into a public seed; only claims landing in a low-probability band from that seed are admitted, like foraging bees finding nectar at scattered flowers. Seed derivation is unbounded, so admission order forms a spiral no attacker can pre-map to harvest cheap slots. Honest agents accumulate durable standing through repeated admission across a trellis of epochs, while attackers must register exponentially many identities per successful slot, paying real compute and registration costs on every failed hash.
